summary: Adds the equivalent of the JOSE typ (type) header parameter to COSE. This brings the benefits of explicit typing, as described in RFC 8725, to COSE objects. Its value syntax is the same as the COSE content type header parameter.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC adds a COSE typ header parameter to identify the type of a complete COSE object. Applications can use it to distinguish object types and reject values that do not fit the expected context.

questions: what is the cose typ header parameter
what is explicit typing in cose
what is the cose typ label value
subtitle: Adds a COSE header parameter that identifies the type of the complete COSE object.

tldr.problem: COSE lacked the JOSE typ parameter for identifying the type of a complete signed or encrypted object.
tldr.mechanism: The new typ parameter uses the content-type value syntax and passes its value from COSE implementations to applications.
tldr.outcome: Applications can use explicit typing to distinguish kinds of COSE objects; the parameter must not appear in unprotected headers.

today: RFC 9596 is a Proposed Standard. The unit metadata records no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Explicit Types for COSE Objects
sections.content:
COSE defines many header parameters that parallel those in JOSE, but it had no equivalent of the JOSE typ parameter. That parameter declares the type of the complete object. RFC 9596 adds the equivalent to COSE, allowing applications to distinguish among kinds of COSE objects.

The value uses the same syntax as the existing COSE content type parameter: an unsigned integer registered in the CoAP Content-Formats registry or a string media type.
sections.plainLanguage: The new parameter labels the complete COSE object, not just its payload. An application can use the label to tell different object types apart.

sections.title: How Applications Use typ
sections.content:
The typ parameter identifies the type of the complete COSE object, while the content type parameter identifies the type of its payload. Use is optional and is intended for cases where an application data structure could contain different kinds of COSE object.

COSE implementations pass the value through to the application without processing it. Application-specific rules decide what to do with it; for example, an application can check for a particular expected media type and reject the object if it differs. The typ parameter MUST NOT be present in unprotected headers.
sections.plainLanguage: The COSE library passes the type value to the application. The application decides whether that value is acceptable, and the parameter cannot be placed in an unprotected header.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: Explicit typing can prevent confusion between different kinds of COSE objects. Applications using it should reject objects whose type value is not expected in that context, and should also reject objects without a type parameter when one is expected.
sections.plainLanguage: Applications can reduce confusion by checking the type they expect. They should reject a missing or unexpected type when their rules require one.

sections.title: IANA Registration
sections.content: IANA registered the typ (type) COSE header parameter with label 16. Its value type is an unsigned integer or text string, and its description is the content type of the complete COSE object.
sections.plainLanguage: The COSE registry now lists the typ parameter and its label. The parameter describes the complete object.
